situation:
You are the customer care manager at AXLEPOINT AUTO PARTS, a five-store auto parts chain two years old and most of the way through its first round of funding. The founder (judge) has asked you to recommend what Axlepoint should do about a delivery promise a counter associate made to three repair shops last week.

To win the shops from a national rival, the associate offered them free same-day courier delivery on any part for a full year. Nobody had authorized that offer, and the shops have already signed. Axlepoint runs one courier van, which manages about twelve same-day runs in a day, and it is now full.

Keeping the promise as it stands fills the van with the three new shops and ends same-day delivery for the garages that have bought from the first store since it opened. Cutting the promise back to two runs a week protects those older accounts and asks three customers to accept less than they were told, days after agreeing to it.

The associate brought in the largest accounts Axlepoint has won this year. The founder (judge) wants your recommendation on what to tell the three shops and on how to handle the associate. The founder (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the founder (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:

Business background is the same as the situation above. A counter associate promised three repair shops free same-day courier delivery on any part for a year without authorization, the shops have signed, and the single courier van that manages about twelve same-day runs in a day is already full.

You have asked the customer care manager (participant) to recommend what Axlepoint tells the three shops, and how the associate who made the promise is handled.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, what has your recommendation changed about how we sell?
